description: Attach/upload file (incl. images) + Repository context as REAL working features, fully testable natively (no external network). Both feed bounded context into the NEXT chat turn by prepending a bounded context block to the user message `content` before send (the pipeline's `content` is a plain String that becomes the User Message text; this keeps run_turn and the streaming flow unchanged). ATTACH: a 📎 control opens the native file dialog (reuse tauri-plugin-dialog); text files have their contents read (new Tauri fs-read command) and included as context; images are included only if the selected model advertises the `vision` capability, else a clear 'this model doesn't support images' notice; attachments show as removable chips. REPOSITORY: a 📁 control picks a local folder and lets the user select a bounded subset of files to include as context, capped in total size, showing what's included. Attachments/repo files are cleared after a successful send (they applied to one turn).
steps: Backend: add a Tauri command `read_text_file(path: String) -> Result<FileContentView, CommandError>` in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs (with a factored `_inner` for tests) that validates the path is non-empty and within a max byte cap (reuse/introduce a MAX_ATTACH_BYTES const, e.g. 256 KiB per file), reads UTF-8 text via std::fs, and returns a display-safe view { path, name, byteLen, text }. Reject binary/oversized/unreadable files with a clear CommandError. For IMAGES, add `read_file_base64(path) -> Result<FileBinaryView, CommandError>` returning { path, name, mimeType, base64, byteLen } with its own cap (e.g. 4 MiB) and a mime guess from the extension. Register BOTH in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs generate_handler! (alongside the existing commands). Add unit tests for the _inner fns (temp files: happy path, oversized -> error, missing -> error, non-utf8 -> error).

Backend: add a command `list_repo_files(dir: String) -> Result<RepoListing, CommandError>` (with `_inner`) that walks a picked directory NON-recursively-unbounded but SENSIBLY: cap the number of returned entries (e.g. 500) and skip common noise (.git, node_modules, target, dist, build, binary files by extension). Return { dir, files: [ { relPath, byteLen } ], truncated: bool }. This lets the UI present a checkbox list to pick a bounded subset; actual content is fetched per-file via read_text_file. Register it and add _inner unit tests (temp dir with a few files + a skipped dir; assert filtering + cap + truncated flag).

IPC + types: add wrappers in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts (readTextFile, readFileBase64, listRepoFiles) and camelCase TS types in frontend/src/types/index.ts (FileContentView, FileBinaryView, RepoListing with its RepoFileEntry) mirroring the Rust view structs. Keep the hand-mirror in sync exactly.

Frontend attachments state: extend the composer (local component state is acceptable, or a small addition to the conversations store if the redesign needs it shared) to hold `attachments: Attachment[]` where each is { kind: 'text'|'image', name, path, byteLen, text? , base64?, mimeType? }. Wire the 📎 control (added as a slot in FEAT-002) to `open()` from @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog (multiple + a filter allowing text and image types), then for each picked path call readTextFile (text) or readFileBase64 (image). For an image, check the SELECTED model's capabilities.vision from the providers store `models` (find the AvailableModel matching the effective route/pin); if vision is false, do NOT attach the image and show a visible non-fatal notice 'This model doesn't support images'. Render attachments as chips with a remove (x) button (aria-label like 'Remove attachment <name>').

Frontend repository picker: wire the 📁 control to `open({ directory: true })`, call listRepoFiles(dir), and present a compact selectable list (checkboxes) of files with a running total byte count and a hard cap (e.g. 128 KiB total across selected repo files); disable selection beyond the cap and show 'X of Y KiB included'. Selected files' contents are fetched via readTextFile and held alongside attachments (kind:'text', tagged as repo context). Show which files are included; allow removal.

Send path: modify the composer submit so that, when attachments/repo files are present, it prepends a BOUNDED, clearly-delimited context block to the trimmed draft before calling sendMessage(content). Format e.g. a leading section: for each text/repo file, a fenced block '### Attached file: <name>
```
<text>
```', and for included images a note that an image named <name> is attached (image bytes handling: for THIS iteration, since run_turn maps only text content into the provider history, include the image as a base64 data note ONLY when vision is supported and document the limitation; do NOT silently drop it - either include it in the content block in a model-appropriate way or show the unsupported notice). Enforce the same total cap on the assembled block. Clear attachments/repo selections after a SUCCESSFUL send (mirror how the per-message override is consumed once).

Do NOT change run_turn / send_message backend semantics: the assembled context travels inside the existing `content` String argument. (If, during implementation, passing large image base64 through content proves unworkable, prefer the text-context path for images-as-notes and clearly document that full multimodal image passing is a follow-up; keep the vision-capability gate + visible notice regardless.)
CSS: add chip + repo-file-list styles to app.css using var(--ah-*) tokens.

Tests: vitest for the composer attach flow (mock @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog open() returning a path or paths, mock the new invoke commands in routeInvoke with well-formed shapes): picking a text file adds a chip and its content is prepended to the sent content; picking an image with a vision-capable selected model attaches it; picking an image with a NON-vision model shows the 'doesn't support images' notice and does NOT attach; removing a chip drops it; attachments clear after send. vitest for the repo picker (mock open({directory:true}) + listRepoFiles): selecting files respects the cap and includes their content on send. Rust _inner unit tests as described. Every mounting test mocks ALL invoke commands (including the new ones) and initializes any new store fields in resets.
acceptance_criteria: A 📎 Attach control opens the native file dialog; selecting a text file reads its contents (via read_text_file) and includes them as context in the next turn, shown as a removable chip.
Selecting an image attaches it ONLY when the selected model's Capabilities.vision is true; otherwise a clear visible 'this model doesn't support images' notice is shown and the image is not attached.

A 📁 Repository control picks a folder, lists a bounded/filtered set of files (skipping .git/node_modules/target/etc, capped count with a truncated flag), lets the user select a subset within a total size cap, and includes the selected files' contents as context; what's included is visible and removable.
Attachments and repo selections are cleared after a successful send (they apply to exactly one turn); the assembled context block is size-capped.

New Tauri commands (read_text_file, read_file_base64, list_repo_files) are registered in generate_handler!, have IPC wrappers and camelCase TS types, and pass _inner unit tests (happy + oversized + missing + filtered/cap cases).
run_turn/send_message backend flow is unchanged (context rides inside the existing content String); no regression to threaded chat or send-failure visibility.
Frontend vitest + Rust crate tests pass; tsc/eslint/prettier clean (or CI-only with exhaustive manual review if tooling absent offline).
verification: Run `cargo test -p tauri-app` for the new _inner tests IF the tauri-app crate can be built in-sandbox; it CANNOT (needs crates.io) so this gate is CI-only - do exhaustive manual self-review of the command bodies and confirm registration in lib.rs, IPC wrapper, and TS type parity. Any pure-logic helpers (path filtering, cap enforcement) that can live in a host-verifiable crate should be unit-tested there instead.

Run the frontend vitest suite covering the attach + repository flows; confirm pass. If node_modules absent in-sandbox, CI-only: manually verify the dialog mock, invoke mocks, vision-gate branch, cap logic, and clear-after-send.
tsc/eslint/prettier checks clean (or CI-only with manual review).
